title: Soft Landfall Regional Shepherd: probabilistic geo-pinning with capacity escrow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In peak or degraded conditions we observe noisy failovers where traffic is aggressively ejected from a region and floods another region causing cascading latency spikes and quota exhaustion. Existing geo-pin / latency fallback policies are deterministic and can cause cliff-like capacity transitions.

Goal: Implement a probabilistic, capacity-aware regional steering controller (the 'Soft Landfall Regional Shepherd') that: (1) prefers low-latency region candidates, (2) applies soft geo-pinning with a probabilistic keep-rate per token/request, and (3) uses an escrowed capacity credit pool per region to avoid sudden overcommitments. The controller should integrate with circuit breakers and load-shedding to preserve SLOs and enable graceful multi-region failover.

Scope: routing decision logic, capacity escrow accounting, circuit-breaker integration, local cache-awareness hooks, rollout canary and observability dashboards. Does not include UI surface changes (Console) in this ticket; Console telemetry wiring will be a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes a policy config allowing: latency preference weight, geo_soft_pin_keep_rate (0-1), escrow_window (seconds), escrow_share_threshold (percentage)
At <10% simulated regional capacity loss, >= 90% of requests stay within home region when keep_rate=0.9 and latencies within SLO
If region capacity falls below escrow_share_threshold, controller diverts new traffic gradually (probabilistically) and triggers per-region circuit breaker if backed-off rate > configured threshold
No single region should observe >25% QoS regression when another region loses 30% capacity under canary traffic (50k RPS synthetic) during rollout
End-to-end integration tests that exercise failover, hedge, and load-shed paths pass in CI with deterministic seeds
design_decisions: Use probabilistic keep-rate instead of strict pin/no-pin to smooth traffic transitions and keep KV cache warm paths intact
Maintain a per-region escrow ledger with two counters (committed_credit, pending_release) to avoid double-counting; ledger updates are eventual but bounded by escrow_window
Prefer latency-weighted scoring for candidate selection; capacity headroom is applied as a multiplicative penalty in the score (score *= headroom_factor)

Circuit breakers live in the region agent and are tripped by sustained token-level backlog and elevated tail-latency percentiles (95th/99th). The shepherd subscribes to circuit-breaker state via the control plane stream
Load shedding uses priority tiers: premium traffic hedges to alternate regions earlier; best-effort clients subject to probabilistic shedding when global backpressure exceeds threshold
tradeoffs: Probabilistic routing increases variance in per-request locality but reduces cliff failures; adds complexity to debugging (we will add correlation ids and sample traces)
Escrow adds bookkeeping overhead and slight delay in releasing capacity; prevents oversubscription at cost of temporary conservative utilization
Eventual consistency for escrow/ledgers limits instantaneous accuracy but reduces cross-region synchronization traffic compared to a central lock service
More conservative defaults reduce throughput for short periods during incidents but improve SLO stability
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in CI (feature-flag guarded).
2) Canary in single non-critical region serving 2% of traffic for 48h with synthetic failure injection (simulate -20% GPU capacity). Monitor SLI deltas.
3) Gradual ramp to 10% across two regions, enable escrow with small window (30s) and keep_rate=0.95. Observe KV cache hit changes and tail latency.
4) Enable cross-region canary with synthetic blast where one region is artificially drained to validate circuit-breaker + shed behaviors.
5) Full rollout behind config toggle; monitor for 72h before enabling conservative default widening (reduce keep_rate if needed).
Rollback: revert feature toggle or set keep_rate=1.0 (forces pinning) to return to deterministic behavior
observability: Per-region escrow metrics: committed_credit, pending_release, escrow_consumption_rate
SLO-aligned SLIs: p99 latency per region, request_error_rate, shed_rate_by_priority
Dashboards: Multi-region 'shepherd' overview and incident drill-down with sample traces and request route annotations
test_plan: Deterministic simulator that replays real traffic traces and injects region capacity losses; seeds used to verify probabilistic decisions reproducibly
Chaos test: kill region N replicas and assert that no downstream region exceeds configured headroom for >5 minutes
Load test: synthetic 50k RPS with mixed priorities to exercise escrow accounting under sustained load
E2E canary smoke runs that validate rollback path and ensure no token loss during transitions
